added_lemmas.statement: For a finite-dimensional convex body supplied with rationally encoded inner and outer radius bounds, polynomial-time weak membership and rational approximate-value oracles permit weak constrained convex-function minimization in oracle-polynomial time.  The output accuracy enters the running time through its logarithm; the returned point and value may be chosen rational.

source.locator: Theorem (4.3.13), pages 113--114, together with Definition (2.1.16), page 53, the oracle-polynomial convention on page 55, and Problem (2.1.22), page 56
source.verbatim_statement: Output: A vector \(y\in S(K,\varepsilon)\) such that \(f(y)<f(x)+\varepsilon\) for all \(x\in S(K,-\varepsilon)\).

attestation.note: Verified against the primary PDF at the stated locations. Theorem (4.3.13) takes a positive rational accuracy \(\varepsilon\), a centered convex body \((K;n,R,r,a_0)\) given by weak membership, and a globally defined convex function \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) whose oracle, for rational \(x\) and positive rational \(\delta\), returns rational \(t\) with \(|f(x)-t|<\delta\). Definition (2.1.16) expands centeredness as rational data with \(B(a_0,r)\subseteq K\subseteq B(0,R)\). Problem (2.1.22) specifies that the returned vector is rational, and page 55 makes oracle-polynomial time polynomial in the body's rational encoding and the further inputs, hence logarithmic in inverse binary accuracy. The displayed output sentence is transcribed from Theorem (4.3.13), with notation normalized to LaTeX. One further call to the stated value oracle at the rational output supplies a rational approximate objective value to any requested rational accuracy.

proposed.citation: Grötschel, Martin, László Lovász, and Alexander Schrijver. 1988. Geometric Algorithms and Combinatorial Optimization. Algorithms and Combinatorics 2. Berlin: Springer-Verlag.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The primary PDF identifies Algorithms and Combinatorics 2 as the series volume; it does not identify the 1988 book as a second edition. This replacement makes the bibliography agree with the cited primary source.

prose_updates.related_work: BairdBohrenMcIntoshOzler2018 provides the motivating fixed-count randomized-saturation design and its direct and spillover analysis, but not an unrestricted finite-population minimax estimator or a bit-certified joint design algorithm. AronowSamii2017 supplies exposure mappings, exposure-probability bookkeeping, and design-based estimation under general interference; the present paper instead optimizes jointly over every measurable estimator and every feasible correlated exact-count design. HudgensHalloran2008, BasseFeller2018, and JiangImaiMalani2023 develop the design-based two-stage causal framework without the present all-estimator finite saddle characterization. Bai2023 proves complete randomization by permutation-invariance group averaging for a fixed invariant estimator; here group averaging reduces the entire design--estimator--nature game and retains arbitrary correlated saturation actions. CaiPougetAbadieAiroldi2022 optimizes randomized and deterministic saturation designs for a specified difference-in-means estimator under linear interference, whereas the present criterion is worst-case finite-population squared error over all bounded schedules and all measurable estimators. Kallus2021 establishes mixed-strategy design optimality at a general decision-theoretic level, while the present result constructs and weakly optimizes the exact rational observation-hypergraph quotient. The accepted-bank paper \texttt{exp\_multiarm\_secondorder\_minimax\_frontier\_v1} supplies the finite unrestricted response-orbit minimax and rational-program certificate architecture in the no-interference setting. The present paper inherits that finite minimax architecture, but adds the exact-count higher-order observation hypergraph, the quotient of arbitrary correlated saturation-label actions, the stabilizer-weighted exact kernel, the conditional-uniformity reduction, and a total zero-face-safe decoder with a bit-certified compiler. Hull2026 and SudijonoDobribanTchetgenTchetgen2026 supply endpoint reductions in no-interference experiments, whereas the present compiler covers bounded anonymous saturation interference, arbitrary correlated first-stage laws, boundary treated counts, and label-constant menus. KandirosHarshawSavje2026 studies a pairwise conflict-graph experiment; here every interior exact-count cell yields \(h+1\) same-arm coordinates whose \(h\)-subsets are all observable although the full set is not, so no pairwise graph represents the compatibility complex.

sampling_model.overlap: The general endpoint, orbit-game, frontier, and compiler results allow every feasible count \(0\le r_{q,a}\le q\), including pure-control, pure-treatment, and label-constant menus. A local condition \(1\le r_{q,a}<q\) is used only to produce the higher-order observation obstruction for that realized cluster-label cell. The strict-separation and complement-symmetry specializations directly fix \(r_{3,1}=1\) and \(r_{3,2}=2\); their proofs check \(0<r_{3,a}<3\) and \(r_{3,1}\ne r_{3,2}\) from those displayed numbers and use no global interiority or saturation-variation assumption. Optimal designs may assign zero probability to labels or assignment orbits.

prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The compiler guarantee is polynomial in the displayed orbit-program size for fixed \(K\) and \(b\); it does not make the constant-size response alphabet small in practice and is not a strongly polynomial algorithm. Exact rational arithmetic may produce large certificates even though their bit length is polynomial. The numerical size-three witness remains supported by its separate exhaustive rational verifier, while the compiler theorem supplies the general symbolic kernel construction, global oracle geometry, erosion-correct weak optimization, tolerance accounting, and decoder proof rather than a new numerical rerun. The strict separation is a finite-game, contrast-neighborhood result; no topology on observable laws or asymptotic experiment sequence is part of the theorem.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Endpoint completeness, the exact orbit game, and the bit-certified compiler cover every rational feasible table \(0\le r_{q,a}\le q\), including pure-control, pure-treatment, and label-constant treated-count menus. Hypergraph nonrepresentability is local: it follows whenever a realized cluster-label cell has \(1\le r_{q,a}<q\), with no claim for a table consisting only of boundary cells. The independent-saturation result is a finite primal-dual feasibility and positive-support saddle characterization, not an elementary closed-form classification. The compiler returns rational weakly optimal certificates and a total continuous estimator; it does not claim exact rational optimizers or a separation as the number of clusters tends to infinity. The strict advantage is only the certified two-cluster exact-count game and its stated infinite rational contrast neighborhood. It does not claim robustness in an ambient observable-law topology, nondegenerate superpopulation conditional support or variance, positive region mass, or asymptotic persistence; those would be different strengthening projects, not premises of the stated finite minimax inequality.

statement_notes.justification: This is the lossless finite reduction for every feasible exact-count menu, including pure-control, pure-treatment, and label-constant menus, while retaining the full higher-order observation hypergraph.
statement_notes.gap: The accepted-bank paper \texttt{exp\_multiarm\_secondorder\_minimax\_frontier\_v1} already supplies an unrestricted finite response-orbit minimax game and rational-program certificates without interference. What is added here is the exact-count higher-order observation hypergraph, the arbitrary correlated saturation-label action quotient, its stabilizer-weighted exact kernel, conditional-uniform subset randomization, and the total decoder and bit-certified compiler. The endpoint reductions of SudijonoDobribanTchetgenTchetgen2026 and Hull2026 likewise do not supply those interference-specific objects.
statement_notes.consumer: BairdBohrenMcIntoshOzler2018's saturation shares can be chosen against exact bounded-schedule risk while simultaneously selecting a nonlinear analysis rule.

statement_notes.justification: This is a self-contained certified separation between unrestricted correlated saturation and common-probability independent saturation inside the explicitly defined finite exact-count game, with robustness only over the stated rational contrast neighborhood.
statement_notes.gap: The theorem is not a refutation of Hull2026, whose result is for no interference, or CaiPougetAbadieAiroldi2022, which optimizes a specified estimator under a linear interference model. It instead proves that the two design classes have different unrestricted minimax values in this finite exact-count saturation game. It makes no ambient observable-law genericity, superpopulation nondegeneracy, or asymptotic-persistence claim.
statement_notes.consumer: The result supplies a concrete finite-population reason for BairdBohrenMcIntoshOzler2018-style trials to consider correlated saturation labels when robust worst-case mean-squared error is the design criterion.

statement_notes.justification: This gives an exact finite test for when common-probability independent saturation loses nothing, including equality of primal risk on every positive least-favorable-prior support orbit.
statement_notes.gap: Bai2023 uses permutation invariance to establish complete randomization for a fixed invariant estimator, and CaiPougetAbadieAiroldi2022 optimizes a specified difference-in-means estimator under linear interference. Neither gives the present if-and-only-if positive-support saddle characterization for unrestricted estimators and exact-count interference. AronowSamii2017 supplies the exposure-probability framework for design-based inference, not this joint minimax design characterization.
statement_notes.consumer: A trial planner can test whether ordinary independent cluster saturation is certified minimax before adopting a correlated mechanism.
